newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs up slightly on dealers' buying of cash bonds.
newsitem.headline: JGBs up slightly on dealers' buying of cash bonds.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract was slightly higher by midday on Friday due to dealers' short-covering of the 190th to 196th JGBs, traders said.
Some market players may be buying the 190th JGB in anticipation of its inauguration as the new cash JGB benchmark, which is expected to take place soon, traders said.
The arrests on Thursday of four Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank (DKB) officials on suspicion of violating the Commercial Code has had little impact on JGBs so far, traders said.
The September stood at 122.73 by midday, up slightly from Thursday's close of 122.68.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.515 percent as of 0229 GMT, down slightly from Thursday's close of 2.520 percent.
Traders said the market was quiet during the morning, due to a lack of strong trading incentives and caution ahead of the release of key U.S. May jobs data later in the day.
"There is really nothing going on today, except buy backs by dealers who have been stuck with short positions," a foreign bank trader said.
Dealers have been left with short positions on the 190th to 196th JGBs after selling the cash bonds to investors recently.
"Investors were detected buying long-term cash JGBs yesterday. There has also been some switch overs from the 182nd to the 190th JGBs," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.

The 190th JGB will take over the benchmark mantle after its turnover exceeds that of the current benchmark 182nd JGB over a certain amount of time, said Takeshi Naito, assistant general manager of the market intelligence unit at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd's bond department.
Turnover of the 190th JGB will probably have to exceed that of the 182nd JGB for at least several days in order for the market to consider the 190th as the new benchmark, Naito said.
"The cash JGB issue with the greatest turnover becomes the benchmark, but there is no clear rule about when a benchmark shift becomes official," he said.
Although demand for the 190th is likely to increase in the near-term, the benchmark shift will probably have little overall impact on the market's direction, Naito said.
The 190th JGB yield stood at 2.625 percent as of 0254 GMT, unchanged from Thursday's close.
The arrest of four DKB officials on Friday has had little effect on JGBs so far, traders said.

"If the same thing had happened to a smaller bank, it may have reignited concerns about the financial system, but so far it (the arrests) has not been a very prominent topic in the JGB market," the trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
Tokyo prosecutors said on Thursday they had arrested four officials of one of Japan's top commercial banks, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, on suspicion of loaning 11.78 billion yen to a racketeer.
